THE REPO VALIDATOR NOW FAILS ON FIVE ROWS AND A HUMAN MUST FIX IT, NOT THIS RUN. validate.py reports FAIL '4 badges' for s035-s039: host 'arabnews.com' matches nothing in badge_map. That is exactly the state STEP 7 prescribes for an unmapped host - badge Press, domain appended to unmapped_domains.json, no review_flag - but validate.py treats any unmapped host as a hard failure rather than a worklist item. The five rows carry the Reuters wire of 14 August on French, German, Polish and Romanian maize, which is the single most important EU story of the week. It was searched for on mapped hosts twice (world-grain.com, graincentral.com, agriland.ie, fwi.co.uk, farminguk.com, freshplaza.com, dtnpf.com, agweb.com, farmersguardian.com, barchart.com) and appears on none of them; the only reachable copies are unmapped syndication surfaces (arabnews.com, wtvbam.com, whtc.com, wtaq.com, wiky.com). badge_map.json was NOT edited, per STEP 7. A human should either add arabnews.com to badge_map Press, or teach validate.py to consult unmapped_domains.json.

REUTERS AND BLOOMBERG REMAIN UNREACHABLE BY THIS AGENT. reuters.com and theguardian.com are explicitly refused by the search tool's user agent; both are named in STEP 3 pass 2. Coverage of those desks is therefore indirect, via syndication. This is a standing limitation, reported on 2026-08-10 and still true.

raw.githubusercontent.com WAS UNREACHABLE. Every raw URL was refused by the fetch tool before leaving the sandbox ('URL not in provenance set') - a tool-side allowlist, not an HTTP status from GitHub, so no status code or x-deny-reason exists to report. The git clone route worked and all eight state files were read. Worth a human check on whether raw fetching is expected to work at all from this agent.
TWELVE SERIES NOW HAVE MORE THAN ONE READING AND NO LABEL. Listed in full under series_needing_labels below. Each is chartable:false and stays off Tab 2 until a human writes a label.

ONE ROW WITH A TABULAR RATHER THAN PROSE QUOTE: s026 (Kansas winter wheat, 191.4 mn bu, -44.8% YoY). The verbatim_quote is the NASS briefing table row, since that briefing publishes state figures only in tables. Carries a review_flag. Kept because it is the sharpest state-level fall in the report.

ONE ROW WHOSE QUOTE ONLY PARTLY SUPPORTS ITS FIGURE: the GB potato wholesale price. The source says 'more than 40%', an open-ended lower bound; 40 was recorded with the qualifier in the unit and a review_flag. It merged into a005, which already carried the same figure, so no new row was created.
ONE FIGURE DELIBERATELY LEFT UNQUANTIFIED: s036 (French maize, Expana/Argus). 'Less than 7 million tons' is a bound, not a value, and converting it would be inferring a number.
NO ROW HAS AN EVENT_DATE MORE THAN A YEAR BEFORE ITS PUBLISHED_DATE. The largest gap is 16 days (s015, JRC, event 2026-07-31, published 2026-08-12).

NO KEY COLLISIONS. All seven unquantified rows took fresh fortnight keys; no suffixing was needed. The three Environment Agency unquantified rows were deliberately given distinct impact_class values (farmer_livelihood, yield, food_security) so that three genuinely different facts from one report on one date would not collide on a single 2026-08-B key - the failure mode that nearly lost three India rows.

PRE-EXISTING VALIDATOR WARNINGS UNCHANGED BY THIS RUN: the j022/a004 exempt duplicate key, the 2026-08-09 summary's 59 id-less notable_numbers, and three manifest entries (SA Crop Estimates Committee, ICCO, GB Potatoes) whose last_publication is still null so the silence check cannot fire.

month was set from published_date for all 45 new rows, which is the dominant convention in the corpus (17 exceptions against 49 for the event_date rule). All 45 therefore land in the 2026-08 shard; the July shard changed only because three merges landed on July rows.
Shards were derived by filtering all.json on the month field after all inserts and merges, never from the insert list, and then verified field-for-field against all.json.
